title: Decoding tumour phenotype by noninvasive imaging using a quantitative radiomics approach

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Decoding tumour phenotype by noninvasive imaging using a quantitative radiomics approach》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Human cancers exhibit strong phenotypic differences that can be visualized noninvasively by medical imaging.

evidence.text: Human cancers exhibit strong phenotypic differences that can be visualized noninvasively by medical imaging.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Decoding tumour phenotype by noninvasive imaging using a quantitative radiomics approach》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】Here we present a radiomic analysis of 440 features quantifying tumour image intensity, shape and texture, which are extracted from computed tomography data of 1,019 patients with lung or head-and-neck cancer.

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】We find that a large number of radiomic features have prognostic power in independent data sets of lung and head-and-neck cancer patients, many of which were not identified as significant before.

evidence.text: Here we present a radiomic analysis of 440 features quantifying tumour image intensity, shape and texture, which are extracted from computed tomography data of 1,019 patients with lung or head-and-neck cancer.
We find that a large number of radiomic features have prognostic power in independent data sets of lung and head-and-neck cancer patients, many of which were not identified as significant before.
